director.chapterArc: Begin in measured tactical triage: Callie prices water against ash, mobility, and the risk of pursuit. Let the bait plan tighten into counted, spatially clear action, then release into Pell’s dry accounting. The middle movement becomes an exact physical investigation of the Edge: painful failure, Katori’s correction, Callie’s practical deduction, and a quiet breakthrough whose resource cost remains real. The secret Ward test adds subdued wonder and complicity with Ines. The northern light’s extinction then changes wonder into deliberate threat; the chapter closes on evidence that the company was watched and measured while it slept.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder warm, grounded, and observational. Pain is breath and mechanics, not anguish; magic is applied physics, not spectacle; danger is understood through distance, direction, and cost. Katori remains flat and authoritative, Pell dry and exact, Ines spare and nearly affectless, and Callie analytical even at moments of discovery. The final word carries recognition of an old danger, not a horror flourish.

cues.delivery: Let the forfeited ash register as a private material loss; keep Callie practical and finish on the irreversibility, not self-pity.
cues.from: "And then we fill both casks and she drinks, and we go. North. In the dark, a mile, two if she'll do it, and we sleep dark. And they're lying in a hollow a long way behind us, round some ash that isn't ours any more." She swallowed. "That's the cost. The ash. We don't get it back."
cues.through: "And then we fill both casks and she drinks, and we go. North. In the dark, a mile, two if she'll do it, and we sleep dark. And they're lying in a hollow a long way behind us, round some ash that isn't ours any more." She swallowed. "That's the cost. The ash. We don't get it back."
cues.reason: Callie names the personal cost of the plan.

cues.delivery: Land the ledger word with quiet finality, as an entry that closes ownership rather than an invitation to mourn.
cues.reason: The single written word makes the sacrifice official.

cues.delivery: Give Otto a hushed flicker of vindication—pleased that his rule proved useful, with no time to celebrate it.
cues.reason: A brief character beat relieves the operational tension.

cues.delivery: Make the clang a clean tactical rupture, then track the husk’s route with controlled spatial precision; danger accelerates attention, not speech.
cues.from: The pail's rusted handle caught on the rim of the tank on the way out, and the whole thing went against the steel with a clang like a bell.
cues.through: Then it found the edge, and came round.
cues.reason: The fifth husk wakes and converts the water operation into immediate threat.

cues.delivery: Filter the blade through Callie’s astonished physical perception, but keep the phenomenon concrete—heat, brightness, distance—not mystical.
cues.from: Callie watched her go. She saw Katori's hand come out of her coat. She saw the grey blade, the length of a forearm, simply be there in her fist, and it seemed to Callie that it was the brightest thing she had ever seen on the plain, brighter than the sunset. It was not light. It was just lit. She could feel it from the board the way you feel a stove across a room.
cues.through: Callie watched her go. She saw Katori's hand come out of her coat. She saw the grey blade, the length of a forearm, simply be there in her fist, and it seemed to Callie that it was the brightest thing she had ever seen on the plain, brighter than the sunset. It was not light. It was just lit. She could feel it from the board the way you feel a stove across a room.
cues.reason: Callie witnesses Katori’s Ember at close range.

cues.delivery: Play Pell’s accounting as dry professional consolation; Callie’s repeated answers stay tired and literal, allowing his final distinction to land lightly.
cues.from: "Well," said Pell beside her, very quietly, after a mile. "There's a Handful of Katori's lying in that mud that I'll never see in my book."
cues.through: "I'm not complaining." Pell flicked the reins. "I'm writing it down. There's a difference, and I've been trying to teach it to Otto for three years."
cues.reason: Pell turns loss into understated ledger humor.

cues.delivery: Let the failed pull become bodily memory: breath vanishes before emotion arrives. Keep the tears involuntary and the broken inhalations intelligible.
cues.through: It was not a no this time. It was worse than that. It was the husk's arm coming round at the height of her chest, all over again, and she could not breathe at all, and she came up off the Edge without deciding to. The grey went out of the hook. She sat on the road with both arms round her ribs and her eyes shut and the tears running out of them, breathing in little pieces.
cues.reason: Callie’s ribs turn a familiar technique into disabling pain.

cues.delivery: Hold still with Callie and make Katori’s lack of visible movement the marvel; repeat the appearances with exact, unornamented rhythm.
cues.from: The blade was in her hand.
cues.through: Then it was gone. Then it was there. Then it was gone.
cues.reason: Katori demonstrates that bodily motion is not the source of the Ember blade.

cues.delivery: Keep Ines utterly sincere and arithmetical; the humor comes from treating failure as useful data, never from teasing Callie.
cues.from: "No," said Ines, from the tailboard, where she was running her thumb down an arrow. "That was nothing."
cues.through: "I'm only counting. That was a nothing." She put the arrow back. "It's a sum. You had one answer that worked and one that didn't. Now you've got two that don't. You're closer."
cues.reason: Ines reframes the failed attempt with characteristically dry logic.

cues.delivery: Allow a small breath of discovery, then describe the Edge as a stable physical result. Otto’s response is involuntary and quiet, not applause.
cues.from:
It came.

It came thin at first
cues.reason: Callie summons the Edge without aggravating her ribs.

cues.delivery: Keep the denial straight and Katori’s prediction matter-of-fact; deliver Callie’s immediate disobedience with dry inevitability.
cues.through: Callie waited till they were all asleep and went behind the wagon and tried it on her own.
cues.reason: The narrative fulfills Katori’s prediction as a restrained comic reversal.

cues.delivery: Make the faint shine intimate proof rather than triumph. Let the long stillness carry Callie’s recalculation and the secrecy of what she has learned.
cues.from: For about two breaths, the old-glass shine was on the back of her hand.
cues.through: Then she went back and lay down on her right side under the wagon, and did not tell anybody, and lay awake with her hand against her chest, feeling her heart go.
cues.reason: Callie privately adapts the Ward and confirms it can work without the drop.

cues.delivery: Keep the night exchange barely above breath: Ines offers witness and discretion, while Callie reports the result with contained wonder.
cues.from: "You did it," said Ines, without turning round. She said it very low.
cues.through: "Then that's a sum done," said Ines.
cues.reason: A genuinely hushed conversation establishes quiet complicity.

cues.delivery: Make the extinction abrupt and absolute. Do not dramatize the light itself; let the newly complete darkness create the threat.
cues.through: It did not flicker. It did not go dim. One moment it was there on the edge of the world, lighting the bottom of the clouds. The next moment it was not, and the dark came all the way down to the grass in the north the way it did in every other direction, and there was nothing there at all.
cues.reason: The fixed northern light disappears without transition.

cues.delivery: Keep Ines and Pell’s logic cool; place the unease on the implication that the darkness is scheduled by an intelligence.
cues.from: "I don't know." Ines was quiet for a moment. "Pell says it isn't broken. He says a thing that goes out at the same time every night isn't broken. It's a decision."
cues.through: "I don't know." Ines was quiet for a moment. "Pell says it isn't broken. He says a thing that goes out at the same time every night isn't broken. It's a decision."
cues.reason: The outage is reclassified from failure to deliberate action.

cues.delivery: Name the creatures with controlled recognition of an old injury. No growl or horror sting—the restraint should imply history and unfinished harm.
cues.through: She said it the way you'd say the name of somebody who had once done you a great harm and whom you had hoped never to see again.
cues.reason: Ines identifies the watchers and reveals the personal weight of the name.
